passage: The tomato originated in western South America, where wild species still grow today. It was first domesticated in Mexico, and Spanish explorers brought it to Europe in the sixteenth century. At first, many Europeans grew tomatoes only as decorative plants, because they belonged to the same family as some poisonous species. In Italy, however, people began cooking with tomatoes relatively early, and by the late seventeenth century tomato sauces appeared in Italian recipe books. Today, China is the world's largest producer of tomatoes, followed by India.

qs.q: Wild tomato species can still be found in South America.
qs.e: «where wild species still grow today» → TRUE.

qs.q: Tomatoes were first domesticated in Spain.
qs.e: El texto dice Mexico: lo contradice → FALSE.

qs.q: Some early Europeans thought tomatoes might be dangerous to eat.
qs.e: Los cultivaban solo como decoración por ser familia de plantas venenosas: es una paráfrasis → TRUE.

qs.q: The first tomato sauce recipe was written by a famous chef.
qs.e: No se habla de ningún chef → NOT GIVEN. Si tienes que inventar, es NOT GIVEN.

qs.q: India produces more tomatoes than any other country.
qs.e: China es el mayor productor; India va segunda → FALSE.

passage: Noise pollution is often overlooked compared with air or water pollution, yet it has measurable effects on health. The World Health Organization has linked long-term exposure to traffic noise with sleep disturbance and a higher risk of heart disease. Children in schools near airports have been found to develop reading skills more slowly than children in quieter areas. Some cities have responded by introducing quieter road surfaces and lowering speed limits at night. In Paris, «noise radars» have been tested to identify vehicles that exceed sound limits, although fines were not issued during the first trial period.

qs.q: Noise pollution receives less attention than other kinds of pollution.
qs.e: «often overlooked compared with air or water pollution» → TRUE.

qs.q: Traffic noise is the main cause of heart disease.
qs.e: Dice que eleva el riesgo, no que sea la causa principal. No se afirma ni se niega → NOT GIVEN.

qs.q: Children near airports learn to read more slowly.
Speed limits have been raised at night in some cities.
Drivers were fined during the first trial of Paris's noise radars.
qs.e: «fines were not issued during the first trial» → FALSE.

passage: The first public libraries in the modern sense appeared in the nineteenth century, when governments began to see reading as a way to improve society. In Britain, the Public Libraries Act of 1850 allowed towns to use local taxes to fund libraries, although few towns did so at first. The Scottish-American businessman Andrew Carnegie later paid for the construction of more than 2,500 libraries around the world, on the condition that local authorities provided the land and paid for running costs. Many of these buildings are still in use, though some have been converted into community centers.

qs.q: Modern public libraries began in the nineteenth century.
qs.e: «first public libraries in the modern sense appeared in the nineteenth century» → TRUE.

qs.q: Most British towns built libraries immediately after 1850.
qs.e: «few towns did so at first» → FALSE.

qs.q: Carnegie also paid for the daily running of his libraries.
qs.e: Las autoridades locales pagaban «running costs» → FALSE.

qs.q: Carnegie libraries were built in more than twenty countries.
qs.e: Dice «around the world» pero no da el número de países → NOT GIVEN.

qs.q: Some Carnegie library buildings now serve a different purpose.

passage: Desalination, the process of removing salt from seawater, has become an important source of drinking water in dry regions. The most common method today is reverse osmosis, in which seawater is pushed at high pressure through membranes that block salt. Although the technology has become more energy-efficient over the past three decades, it still requires considerably more energy than treating river or ground water. Another concern is brine, the highly salty water left over after the process, which can harm marine life if it is released without proper dilution. Researchers are investigating ways to extract useful minerals from brine, but these methods are not yet widely used.

qs.q: Reverse osmosis is currently the most widely used desalination method.
qs.e: «The most common method today is reverse osmosis» → TRUE.

qs.q: Desalination now uses less energy than treating river water.
The cost of desalinated water has fallen by half since the 1990s.
qs.e: Habla de energía, no de precio ni de «la mitad» → NOT GIVEN.

qs.q: Brine can be harmful to sea creatures.
Extracting minerals from brine is already common practice.

passage: Honey is one of the few foods that can last for a very long time without spoiling. Archaeologists have found pots of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that were still edible. Honey stays fresh because it contains very little water and is naturally acidic, which prevents bacteria from growing. Bees make honey from the nectar of flowers, and the color and taste depend on which flowers the bees visit. A single bee produces only about one twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in its whole life.

qs.q: Honey found in Egyptian tombs could still be eaten.
Honey contains a large amount of water.
Dark honey is healthier than light honey.
qs.e: Solo se dice que el color depende de las flores; nada de salud → NOT GIVEN.

qs.q: One bee makes less than a teaspoon of honey during its life.
qs.e: 1/12 de cucharadita es menos de una → TRUE.

passage: For decades, the dominant view in linguistics was that children learn grammar mainly through an innate language ability. More recent research, however, emphasizes the role of statistical learning: infants appear to track how often certain sounds and words occur together. In one well-known experiment, eight-month-old babies listened to a stream of invented syllables for just two minutes and afterwards could distinguish «words» that had appeared together frequently from random combinations. Critics argue that such experiments use simplified artificial languages and may not reflect how children acquire real languages. Nevertheless, statistical learning is now widely accepted as at least one important mechanism.

qs.q: The idea of an innate language ability was once the most accepted view.
In the experiment, babies listened to real words for two minutes.
qs.e: Eran «invented syllables», no palabras reales → FALSE.

qs.q: The experiment was repeated with older children.
Some researchers question how well these experiments represent natural learning.
Statistical learning is now considered the only way children learn language.
qs.e: «at least one important mechanism» ≠ el único → FALSE. Ojo a «only», «always», «never».

passage: The bicycle as we know it developed gradually during the nineteenth century. Early versions, introduced around 1817, had no pedals; riders pushed themselves along with their feet. Pedals attached to the front wheel appeared in the 1860s, which led to designs with a very large front wheel to increase speed. These «high-wheelers» were fast but dangerous. The «safety bicycle» of the 1880s, with two wheels of similar size and a chain driving the rear wheel, quickly became popular and gave many women new freedom to travel independently.

qs.q: The earliest bicycles were moved by the rider's feet on the ground.
qs.e: «no pedals; riders pushed themselves along with their feet» → TRUE.

qs.q: High-wheelers were designed to be safer than earlier models.
qs.e: Se diseñaron para la velocidad y eran «dangerous» → FALSE.

qs.q: The safety bicycle used a chain connected to the back wheel.
qs.e: «a chain driving the rear wheel» → TRUE.

qs.q: The safety bicycle was invented by a woman.
qs.e: Se habla de mujeres usuarias, no de quién la inventó → NOT GIVEN.

passage: Mangrove forests grow along tropical coastlines where trees can tolerate salty water. Their tangled roots slow down waves and help protect coastal communities from storms. Mangroves also store large amounts of carbon in their soil, more per hectare than many inland forests. Despite these benefits, a significant proportion of the world's mangroves have been cleared over the last fifty years, mainly for shrimp farms and coastal development. Several countries, including Indonesia and the Philippines, have launched replanting programmes, although not all planted seedlings survive.

qs.q: Mangroves can survive in salty water.
Mangroves store less carbon than most inland forests.
Shrimp farming is one reason for the loss of mangroves.
Indonesia's replanting programme has been the most successful in the world.
qs.e: No hay comparación de éxito → NOT GIVEN.

qs.q: Every seedling planted in these programmes grows into a tree.

passage:
Vertical farming involves growing crops in stacked layers inside buildings, often using LED lights and nutrient-rich water instead of soil. Supporters argue that it allows food to be produced close to cities, reducing transport distances, and that it uses up to ninety percent less water than conventional agriculture because water is recycled. Crops can be grown all year round, unaffected by weather.

However, the method has significant limitations. Electricity for lighting and climate control is expensive, and several vertical farming companies have closed in recent years because they could not make a profit. At present, the technology is mainly suitable for leafy greens and herbs, which grow quickly and are light; staple crops such as wheat or rice would require far too much energy to be practical. Many experts therefore see vertical farming as a complement to traditional farming rather than a replacement.

qs.q: According to the passage, vertical farming saves water because
Why have some vertical farming companies closed?
o: Their crops were affected by bad weather
They could not cover their costs
They could not find enough workers
qs.e: «could not make a profit» por la electricidad.

qs.q: Which crops are currently most suitable for vertical farming?
qs.e: «mainly suitable for leafy greens and herbs».

qs.q: What is the general view of experts mentioned in the passage?
o: Vertical farming will soon replace traditional farming
Vertical farming can support, but not replace, traditional farming
Vertical farming is only useful in deserts

passage:
The concept of «flow», introduced by the psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi, describes a mental state in which a person is fully absorbed in an activity. People in flow often lose track of time and feel a deep sense of satisfaction. Csikszentmihalyi found that flow is most likely when there is a balance between the challenge of a task and the person's skill level. If a task is too easy, people become bored; if it is too difficult, they become anxious.

Flow also requires clear goals and immediate feedback. A rock climber, for example, knows exactly what the next move should be and instantly feels whether it succeeded. Interestingly, Csikszentmihalyi's research showed that people reported flow more often at work than during leisure time, even though they said they would prefer to be doing something else when at work. Passive activities such as watching television rarely produced flow.

qs.q: According to the passage, flow is most likely to occur when
o: challenge and skill are well matched
a person is relaxed and passive
qs.e: «a balance between the challenge of a task and the person's skill level».

qs.q: The example of the rock climber illustrates
o: the need for clear goals and quick feedback
qs.e: Va justo detrás de «clear goals and immediate feedback».

qs.q: What did Csikszentmihalyi find surprising about work?
o: People never experienced flow at work
People experienced flow at work more than in free time
qs.e: «reported flow more often at work than during leisure time».

qs.q: What does the passage suggest about watching television?

passage: The Great Barrier Reef, off the coast of Queensland, Australia, is the world's largest coral reef system. It stretches for more than 2,300 kilometers and can be seen from space. The reef is home to thousands of species of fish, as well as turtles, dolphins and sharks. Tourism connected to the reef supports tens of thousands of jobs in the region. In recent years, rising sea temperatures have caused several mass bleaching events, in which corals lose the algae that give them color and energy. Scientists and the Australian government are working on programmes to reduce pollution from farms and to help corals recover.

passage:
Since the 1990s, many countries have seen a sharp rise in the number of people working from home at least part of the week. Early research focused mainly on productivity, with mixed results: some employees completed more work at home, while others were distracted. More recent studies have turned attention to wellbeing. Remote workers often report greater satisfaction thanks to the absence of commuting, but they are also more likely to feel isolated and to work longer hours, as the boundary between work and personal life becomes unclear.

Many organisations have responded with «hybrid» arrangements, in which staff spend part of the week in the office. The aim is to combine the flexibility of home working with the social contact and spontaneous collaboration of the workplace. However, researchers warn that hybrid systems work best when teams agree on shared office days; otherwise employees may travel to the office only to find their colleagues are absent.

qs.q: What did early research on home working mainly examine?
Which disadvantage of home working is mentioned?
What is the main purpose of hybrid arrangements?

qs.e: «combine the flexibility… with the social contact».

qs.q: According to researchers, hybrid systems are more effective when
o: employees choose their own days freely
teams agree on the same office days
qs.e: «work best when teams agree on shared office days».

B. In 1714, the British government offered a large prize to anyone who could find a practical method of determining longitude. Many scientists believed the solution would come from astronomy.

C. Instead, a self-taught clockmaker named John Harrison spent decades building increasingly accurate clocks that could keep time on a moving ship. By comparing local time with the time at a known place, sailors could calculate their position.

D. Today, satellite systems such as GPS have replaced marine clocks, but the principle is similar: GPS receivers calculate position by measuring tiny differences in the time signals sent by satellites.

passage: The Japanese bullet train, or Shinkansen, began operating in 1964, just before the Tokyo Olympic Games. The first line connected Tokyo and Osaka and reduced the journey time from nearly seven hours to about four. Today, trains on this route travel at up to 285 kilometres per hour. The Shinkansen is famous for its punctuality: the average delay is usually less than one minute. Cleaning teams can prepare a train for its next journey in just seven minutes.

qs.q: The first Shinkansen line ran between Tokyo and ___.
The service started shortly before the ___.
qs.e: «just before the Tokyo Olympic Games». Máximo dos palabras: «Olympic Games».

A train can be cleaned in ___ minutes.
qs.e: «in just seven minutes». Los números cuentan como una palabra.

passage: Octopuses are considered among the most intelligent invertebrates. They have around 500 million neurons, two-thirds of which are located in their arms rather than their brain. This allows each arm to react to its surroundings with a degree of independence. In laboratories, octopuses have learned to open jars and escape from tanks. They are also masters of camouflage: special skin cells called chromatophores allow them to change colour in a fraction of a second, even though octopuses are believed to be colour-blind.

qs.q: Most of an octopus's neurons are found in its ___.
In experiments, octopuses have managed to open ___.

passage: The Dead Sea, located between Jordan and the West Bank, lies more than 400 metres below sea level, making its shores the lowest land on Earth. Its water is almost ten times saltier than the ocean, so people float easily on the surface. No fish can survive there, which is how the lake got its name. Since the 1960s, the water level has been falling by about one metre per year, largely because water from the Jordan River is diverted for farming and drinking.

passage: The placebo effect occurs when patients experience real improvements after receiving a treatment with no active ingredient. Its strength depends on expectations: larger pills, injections and even more expensive-looking packaging tend to produce stronger effects. Surprisingly, some studies have found that placebos can work even when patients are told openly that they are taking a placebo, a phenomenon known as an «open-label» placebo. Researchers believe the ritual of treatment itself, including the attention of a caring doctor, plays an important role.

qs.q: A placebo contains no ___ ingredient.
The strength of the placebo effect depends on patients' ___.
When patients know they are receiving a placebo, it is called an ___ placebo.
The ___ of treatment may be an important factor.

Emperor penguins, the largest species, can dive to depths of over 500 metres. During the Antarctic winter, male emperor penguins keep their eggs warm on their feet for about two months while the females feed at sea. The males huddle together in large groups to protect themselves from the wind.

passage:
The table below shows the percentage of households using solar panels in four countries in 2000, 2010 and 2020.

Spain: 2% / 9% / 21%
Germany: 4% / 15% / 24%
Japan: 3% / 7% / 12%
Egypt: 1% / 2% / 8%

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
model:
The table compares the proportion of households with solar panels in Spain, Germany, Japan and Egypt in 2000, 2010 and 2020.

Overall, solar panel use increased in all four countries over the twenty-year period. Germany had the highest figures throughout, while Egypt consistently had the lowest.

In 2000, solar panels were rare everywhere, ranging from just 1% of households in Egypt to 4% in Germany. Over the next decade, Germany saw the fastest growth, reaching 15%, followed by Spain at 9%. Japan's figure more than doubled to 7%, whereas Egypt's rose only slightly to 2%.

Between 2010 and 2020, the most dramatic increase was in Spain, where the percentage more than doubled to 21%, bringing it close to Germany's 24%. Japan reached 12%, and Egypt, despite starting from a very low base, quadrupled its figure to 8%.

In summary, although all countries expanded their use of solar energy, Germany and Spain stood out with around a fifth or more of households using solar panels by 2020.
tips: Introducción = paráfrasis del enunciado (no copies).
Overview SIN cifras: tendencia general + el mayor/menor.
Agrupa por periodos o por países y compara; no describas cifra por cifra.

passage:
The line graph describes the number of visitors (in thousands) to three museums in a city between 2015 and 2023.

Science Museum: 2015: 400, 2017: 450, 2019: 520, 2020: 150, 2021: 300, 2023: 560
Art Gallery: 2015: 300, 2017: 310, 2019: 320, 2020: 90, 2021: 200, 2023: 290
History Museum: 2015: 250, 2017: 220, 2019: 200, 2020: 60, 2021: 120, 2023: 260

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
model:
The line graph illustrates how many people visited a science museum, an art gallery and a history museum in a city from 2015 to 2023.

Overall, the Science Museum was the most popular attraction throughout the period. All three venues experienced a sharp fall in 2020, followed by a recovery, although only the Science Museum and the History Museum ended the period above their 2015 levels.

Between 2015 and 2019, visitor numbers at the Science Museum rose steadily from 400,000 to 520,000. The Art Gallery remained fairly stable at around 300,000, while the History Museum declined gradually from 250,000 to 200,000.

In 2020, attendance collapsed at all three, falling to 150,000, 90,000 and 60,000 respectively. Numbers then recovered strongly. By 2023, the Science Museum had reached a peak of 560,000, and the History Museum had climbed to 260,000, slightly above its starting point. The Art Gallery, by contrast, recovered to 290,000, just below its 2015 figure.
tips: Usa verbos de tendencia: rose steadily, remained stable, collapsed, recovered.
«respectively» ahorra palabras al dar varias cifras.
Señala la anomalía (2020) en el overview.

passage:
The diagram shows the process of producing paper from recycled materials. Stages: 1) Used paper is collected from homes and offices. 2) It is sorted to remove plastic and metal. 3) The paper is mixed with water and chemicals to make pulp. 4) The pulp is cleaned and ink is removed. 5) The pulp is pressed and dried between large heated rollers. 6) The new paper is rolled up and cut into sheets for delivery.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features. Write at least 150 words.
model:
The diagram illustrates the stages involved in manufacturing new paper from recycled paper.

Overall, the process consists of six main steps, beginning with the collection of used paper and ending with the delivery of new sheets. It combines mechanical stages, such as sorting and pressing, with chemical treatment.

First, used paper is gathered from households and workplaces. It is then sorted carefully so that any plastic or metal items are removed. After this, the paper is combined with water and chemicals to produce pulp.

At the next stage, the pulp is cleaned and the ink is extracted, which ensures that the final product is clean. The pulp is subsequently pressed and dried as it passes between large heated rollers.

Finally, the new paper is wound into large rolls, which are then cut into individual sheets ready to be delivered to customers. In this way, waste paper is transformed into a usable product.
tips: Los procesos se describen en PASIVA: is collected, is sorted.
Secuenciadores: First, then, after this, subsequently, finally.
Overview: número de etapas + principio y fin.

passage:
The bar chart shows how students at a university travel to campus (percentage of students), in 2010 and 2020.

Car: 2010: 40% / 2020: 25%
Bus: 2010: 30% / 2020: 30%
Bicycle: 2010: 10% / 2020: 25%
Walking: 2010: 20% / 2020: 20%

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
model:
The bar chart compares the ways in which university students travelled to campus in 2010 and 2020.

Overall, the car became less popular while cycling grew significantly. The proportions of students who took the bus or walked did not change.

In 2010, the car was the most common means of transport, used by 40% of students. Buses came second at 30%, followed by walking at 20%, while only one in ten students cycled.

By 2020, the situation had changed considerably. Car use had fallen by 15 percentage points to 25%, so the bus became the most popular option, still at 30%. Meanwhile, the share of students cycling had risen sharply from 10% to 25%, making the bicycle as popular as the car. The percentage of students walking to campus remained unchanged at 20%.

In short, the decade saw a clear shift away from cars towards bicycles, with other modes of transport remaining stable.
tips: «percentage points» para diferencias entre porcentajes.
Menciona lo que NO cambia: también es un rasgo principal.
Unas 170 palabras: no hace falta más.

passage:
The pie charts show the average household spending in a country in 1990 and 2020.

1990: Housing 25% · Food 30% · Transport 15% · Education 10% · Leisure 10% · Other 10%
2020: Housing 35% · Food 18% · Transport 15% · Education 14% · Leisure 12% · Other 6%

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
model:
The pie charts illustrate how households in one country divided their spending in 1990 and 2020.

Overall, housing replaced food as the largest category of expenditure, while transport remained the same. Spending on education and leisure grew moderately.

In 1990, food accounted for the biggest share of household budgets at 30%, followed by housing at a quarter. Transport represented 15%, and education, leisure and other expenses each made up 10%.

Thirty years later, the proportion spent on housing had risen to 35%, making it by far the largest item. In contrast, the share devoted to food fell considerably to 18%. Education increased to 14%, and leisure rose slightly to 12%. Transport remained unchanged at 15%, whereas other expenses dropped from 10% to 6%.

In summary, the most notable changes were the growing importance of housing costs and the declining share of income spent on food.
tips: Vocabulario de proporción: accounted for, made up, a quarter, the share devoted to.
Compara el «antes y después» de las categorías que más cambian.
No uses «I think»: Task 1 es descriptiva, sin opinión.

passage:
The two maps show a coastal village in 2000 and today.

2000: a small fishing village with a harbour, fishermen's houses along the beach, a forest to the north, farmland to the east and a single road to the main town.
Today: the harbour has been enlarged into a marina; the fishermen's houses have been replaced by hotels; part of the forest has been cleared for a public park and a car park; the farmland has become a residential area; a new road runs along the coast.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
model:
The maps illustrate the changes that have taken place in a coastal village between 2000 and the present day.

Overall, the village has been transformed from a small fishing community into a tourist and residential area, with significant development along the coast and inland.

In 2000, the village consisted mainly of a harbour and a row of fishermen's houses along the beach. There was a forest to the north and farmland to the east, and only one road connected the village to the main town.

Since then, the harbour has been expanded into a marina, and the fishermen's houses have been demolished and replaced by hotels. To the north, part of the forest has been cleared to make way for a public park and a car park. The farmland to the east has been converted into housing. In addition, a new coastal road has been built.

In summary, natural and agricultural areas have been reduced as tourism and housing have grown.
tips: Mapas = presente perfecto pasivo: has been expanded, have been replaced.
Organiza por zonas (costa, norte, este).
Overview: el cambio general de carácter del lugar.

passage: Some people think that children should start learning a foreign language at primary school, while others believe they should begin in secondary school. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Write at least 250 words.
model:
The age at which children should begin learning a foreign language is a matter of debate. While some argue that it is more effective to wait until secondary school, I believe the benefits of starting in primary school are greater.

Those who favour a later start point out that older children have better developed study skills and a stronger command of their first language. A twelve-year-old can understand grammatical explanations and organise their own learning, so progress may be faster. In addition, primary schools often lack teachers who are fluent in foreign languages, which can lead to poor pronunciation being taught.

On the other hand, young children have clear advantages as language learners. They are generally less afraid of making mistakes, so they are more willing to speak, and they are better at imitating new sounds, which helps them develop more natural pronunciation. Starting early also means that, by the time they leave school, students will have studied the language for many more years, giving them a stronger foundation. Countries such as the Netherlands, where English is introduced early, are known for their high levels of proficiency.

In my opinion, the best approach is to introduce foreign languages in primary school through songs, games and conversation, focusing on listening and speaking rather than grammar. More formal study can then be added in secondary school. This combines the natural confidence of young learners with the analytical skills of older students.

In conclusion, although older learners have certain advantages, I am convinced that an early start, if taught appropriately, gives children the best chance of becoming confident users of a foreign language.
tips: Discuss both views: un párrafo para cada postura + tu opinión clara.
Da tu opinión en la introducción y repítela en la conclusión.
Cada párrafo: idea principal → explicación → ejemplo.

passage: In many cities, traffic congestion is a growing problem. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it? Write at least 250 words.
model:
Traffic congestion has become a serious issue in many cities around the world, wasting time and damaging air quality. This essay will examine the main causes of this problem and suggest some possible solutions.

The most obvious cause is the rising number of private cars. As incomes increase, more families can afford a vehicle, and many people see cars as more comfortable and convenient than public transport. A second cause is urban planning. In many cities, homes, offices and shops are located far apart, so residents have no choice but to travel long distances every day. Poor public transport makes the situation worse, because when buses are slow or unreliable, people naturally choose to drive.

Several measures could help to reduce congestion. Firstly, governments should invest in fast, frequent and affordable public transport, such as metro systems and dedicated bus lanes. Seoul, for example, significantly improved traffic flow after reorganising its bus network. Secondly, cities could introduce congestion charges, requiring drivers to pay to enter the city centre at peak times, as London has done since 2003. Finally, encouraging flexible working hours and remote work would spread journeys more evenly throughout the day.

In conclusion, traffic congestion is caused mainly by growing car ownership, poor urban planning and inadequate public transport. A combination of better transport services, financial incentives and flexible working arrangements offers the most effective way to tackle the problem.
tips: Estructura problema-solución: un párrafo de causas, uno de soluciones.
Empareja cada solución con una causa.
Ejemplos reales (Londres, Seúl) dan peso, pero solo si estás seguro.

passage: Some people believe that university education should be free for all students. Others think students should pay for their own studies. To what extent do you agree or disagree? Write at least 250 words.
model:
Whether university education should be funded by the state or by students themselves is a controversial question. Although free higher education has some drawbacks, I largely agree that it should be available to all students without tuition fees.

The strongest argument for free university education is equality of opportunity. When students must pay high fees, talented young people from low-income families may decide not to apply, or may graduate with heavy debts that limit their choices for years. Making university free ensures that admission depends on ability rather than wealth. Moreover, society as a whole benefits from a well-educated population. Graduates tend to earn higher salaries and therefore pay more tax, and countries need skilled doctors, engineers and teachers to function well.

Critics argue that free education is extremely expensive for governments and that taxpayers who never attended university should not pay for others. They also suggest that students who pay fees take their studies more seriously. These points have some validity, and in practice free systems can lead to overcrowded classes if funding is insufficient.

However, these problems can be addressed. Governments can limit places according to the needs of the economy and require students to maintain good academic results to keep their free place. Countries such as Germany and Norway show that free higher education can be sustainable when it is well managed.

In conclusion, while the cost to the state is considerable, I believe free university education is a worthwhile investment because it promotes fairness and strengthens society in the long term.
tips: «To what extent» pide un grado: «I largely agree…».
Concede el punto contrario y luego responde a él.
Evita frases absolutas; matiza con «tend to», «in practice».

passage: Nowadays many people spend a lot of time on their smartphones. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages? Write at least 250 words.
model:
Smartphones have become an essential part of daily life, and many people spend several hours a day using them. In my view, although heavy smartphone use brings real benefits, the disadvantages are more significant.

There is no doubt that smartphones offer important advantages. They allow people to stay in contact with family and friends wherever they are, which is particularly valuable for those living abroad. They also give instant access to information and services: users can check maps, pay bills, study a language or read the news in seconds. For many people, this saves considerable time.

However, spending too much time on smartphones has serious drawbacks. Firstly, it can harm physical and mental health. Looking at a screen late at night disturbs sleep, and constant notifications make it difficult to concentrate. Studies have linked heavy social media use among teenagers with anxiety and low self-esteem. Secondly, excessive phone use can damage relationships. It is common to see families sitting together at dinner while each person looks at their own screen, which reduces real conversation.

Overall, the problem is not the technology itself but how much it is used. The benefits of smartphones can be enjoyed in a limited amount of time, while the negative effects increase as usage grows.

In conclusion, I believe that the disadvantages of spending a lot of time on smartphones outweigh the advantages, and people should make a conscious effort to limit their screen time.
tips: «Do advantages outweigh…?» exige respuesta clara: sí o no.
Dedica más espacio al lado que defiendes.
Conclusión con recomendación breve.

passage: Some people think that the best way to protect the environment is for individuals to change their behaviour. Others believe that governments and large companies must take the main responsibility. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Write at least 250 words.
model:
Environmental damage is one of the most urgent challenges of our time, and there is disagreement about who should take the lead in addressing it. While individual action is important, I believe governments and large companies must carry the main responsibility.

Supporters of individual responsibility argue that environmental problems are ultimately caused by consumer choices. If millions of people reduce their energy use, avoid unnecessary flights and buy fewer disposable products, the combined effect can be considerable. Personal action also sends a message to businesses, since companies respond to changing demand.

However, there are limits to what individuals can achieve. Many people cannot afford electric cars or energy-efficient homes, and in some areas there is no reliable public transport to replace driving. Furthermore, a large proportion of emissions comes from industry, power generation and transport systems that individuals do not control. Governments, on the other hand, can introduce laws, taxes and investments that affect entire countries. For example, setting strict standards for vehicle emissions or investing in renewable energy changes behaviour on a massive scale. Large companies can also redesign products and supply chains to reduce waste.

In my opinion, the most effective approach is for governments to create the conditions that make environmentally friendly choices easy and affordable, and for companies to be held accountable for their impact. Individual actions are valuable, but they work best within this framework.

In conclusion, both individuals and institutions have a role to play, but the scale of the problem means that governments and corporations must take the lead.
tips: Presenta la postura contraria con justicia antes de rebatirla.
Usa «Furthermore», «on the other hand», «In my opinion».
No te quedes en el medio sin decidir: el examinador quiere tu postura.

passage: In some countries, the average age of the population is increasing. What problems will this cause for individuals and society? Suggest some measures that could reduce these problems. Write at least 250 words.
model:
Many countries, including Japan, Italy and Spain, are experiencing a rapid increase in the average age of their populations. This trend creates challenges for both individuals and society, but there are measures that could reduce its impact.

For society, the most serious problem is economic. As the proportion of older people grows, there are fewer working-age adults paying taxes to support pensions and healthcare. Health systems face rising demand for long-term care, which is extremely costly. In addition, labour shortages can develop in sectors such as construction, agriculture and nursing.

For individuals, an ageing population can mean pressure on families. Adult children may need to care for elderly parents while also working and raising their own children. Older people themselves may suffer from loneliness, especially if they live alone or far from their families.

Several measures could help. Firstly, governments could gradually raise the retirement age and encourage flexible employment, allowing healthy older people to continue working part-time. This would increase tax revenue and keep people socially active. Secondly, investment in preventive healthcare and community programmes would help older citizens stay independent for longer. Finally, policies that support families, such as affordable childcare, and well-managed immigration could help to balance the working population.

In conclusion, an ageing population puts pressure on public finances, families and older people themselves. However, by extending working lives, promoting healthy ageing and supporting a larger workforce, governments can reduce these problems significantly.
tips: Pregunta doble: responde a las DOS partes (problemas + medidas).
Separa problemas para la sociedad y para individuos: es lo que pide.
Cada medida, con su efecto («This would…»).

passage: Some people prefer to live in a big city, while others prefer to live in the countryside. Discuss the advantages of both and give your own opinion. Write at least 250 words.
model:
People have different preferences about where to live. Some are attracted by the energy of big cities, while others value the peace of rural areas. Both have clear advantages, but in my opinion city life is more suitable for most young people.

Living in a big city offers many opportunities. There are more jobs, especially in sectors such as technology, finance and the arts, and salaries are often higher. Cities also have better public services, including hospitals, universities and public transport, so residents do not need a car. In addition, there is a wide range of cultural activities, from museums to sports events, and it is easier to meet people from different backgrounds.

On the other hand, the countryside has its own benefits. The air is cleaner, there is less noise, and people can enjoy nature every day. Housing is usually much cheaper, so families can afford larger homes with gardens. Rural communities are often close-knit, and neighbours know and help one another, which can create a strong sense of belonging.

Personally, I believe that a city is the better choice for young adults who are studying or building a career, because of the opportunities it offers. However, many people may prefer to move to the countryside later in life, when they value space and tranquillity more than excitement.

In conclusion, cities and the countryside both offer an attractive lifestyle, and the best choice depends largely on a person's stage of life.
tips: Pide ventajas de AMBOS: no hables de desventajas.
Opinión matizada por etapa de la vida: original y fácil de defender.
Vocabulario: close-knit, tranquillity, a sense of belonging.

passage: Many museums and historical sites are mainly visited by tourists, not by local people. Why is this the case? What can be done to attract more local visitors? Write at least 250 words.
model:
It is often observed that museums and historical sites attract far more tourists than local residents. This essay will discuss the reasons for this and suggest ways to encourage more local people to visit.

One reason is that residents tend to take nearby attractions for granted. Because these places are always available, local people assume they can visit them at any time and therefore keep postponing it. Tourists, by contrast, have a limited time and specifically plan to see famous sights. Another reason is cost. Entrance fees that seem reasonable to a visitor on holiday may appear expensive to a family who would have to pay them repeatedly. Finally, many museums have permanent exhibitions that rarely change, so locals who have already visited once see no reason to return.

There are several ways to address this situation. Museums could offer free or discounted entry to residents, perhaps on one day each month. Organising temporary exhibitions, evening events and workshops for children would give local people new reasons to come back. Schools could also include regular visits to local museums in their programmes, helping young people develop an interest in their own heritage. Finally, using social media to promote events in the local language would make residents feel that these places are for them, not only for visitors.

In conclusion, local people often ignore nearby museums because they take them for granted, find them expensive or feel the exhibitions never change. Discounts, new events and educational programmes could make these institutions an active part of community life.
tips: Pregunta directa doble (why + what): dos cuerpos claros.
Empareja cada solución con una causa.
Conclusión que resume causas y soluciones.
